title: Helix HCO+ J=1–0 published component fits

citation.label: Zeigler, Zack, Woolf & Ziurys (2013), ApJ 778, 16, Table 1 and §§2–3

tracer.emissionPhase: molecular gas; distinct from the inner [O III] ionized shell

coordinates.evidence: Paper §2 and Table 1 footnote a identify this central-star origin; CDS ReadMe Note 1 agrees. Figures 1 and 3 were visually inspected: RA offset decreases toward west/right, declination increases toward north/up. Use the published map angular offsets directly: xWest=−oRA, yNorth=oDE; apply no second cos(declination) scaling. The paper describes 70 arcsec beam-sized spacing and 35 arcsec half-beam spacing. Its J2000 anchor is retained verbatim; no ICRS transformation or recentering was performed.

velocity.definitionNote: The paper and CDS identify Local Standard of Rest velocities but do not explicitly name the LSRK/LSRD convention. Keep the published LSR label; do not silently equate this with an unrelated cube frame.

publishedHeliocentricConversion.source: Paper §3, page 2 explicitly states V_LSR = V_hel + 3.12 km/s. This source-specific relation is available for explicitly framed model priors; the loader preserves every measured V_LSR unchanged.

velocity.uncertaintyNote: Table 1 contains Gaussian-fit centroids, FWHM and intensities, but no per-component errors or covariance. Null errors mean unreported, never zero uncertainty. The 1.68 km/s spectral resolution, fitted FWHM and 0.1 km/s printed precision are not centroid errors. Broad and unresolved blends limit interpretation.

instrument.telescope: Arizona Radio Observatory 12 m, Kitt Peak
instrument.source: Paper §2 and Figure 1 caption: 2008 November–2013 March; 250/500 kHz backends, 70 arcsec FWHM beam. The published map uses 1.68 km/s resolution. Northwest sampling at 35 arcsec is half a beam, not 35 arcsec independent spatial resolution; neighboring pointings overlap.

intensity.upperLimitMeaning: The '<' flag is an upper limit on line intensity, not velocity. Paper §2 describes observations to about 20 mK at 3 sigma rms; limits vary by table row. Preserve each listed threshold without inventing a line centroid, width or per-row noise variance.
intensity.source: Paper §2 gives T_R = T_R*/eta_c with eta_c=0.89. The loader keeps published T_R* in mK and applies no efficiency conversion. These are line peak temperatures, not RGB emission weights or velocity-independent integrated intensities.

broadLineNotice.source: Paper §3 notes that lines broader than 15 km/s likely contain unresolved components. The loader marks them for inspection and keeps them; it does not split, suppress or relabel them as separate physical features.

limitations: The exact CDS table has 327 rows: 279 detected Gaussian components at 170 distinct offsets, plus 48 upper-limit offsets, for 218 pointings. The paper states 219 pointings and 168 detections. This discrepancy is unresolved; the loader reports the actual pinned table counts and never pads or changes rows to agree with prose.

No (0,0) row exists in this table, although the paper describes a central nondetection. Missing central coverage and the largely unobserved central region are not zero emission; the unlisted central limit cannot be used numerically.

The CDS Objects section gives a different catalogue lookup coordinate, 22:29:38.54 −20:50:13.6. It is not the Table 1 offset origin and must not replace it. Translate the recorded origin when comparing a separately registered image frame; do not silently recenter the data.

Each row is a published Gaussian component fit, not an original channel spectrum or a point at known depth. Repeated offsets are multiple fitted components in one 70 arcsec beam; hold out whole pointings, not components from the same spectrum. Adjacent 35 arcsec pointings are correlated through overlapping beams.

The table covers coarse molecular material in the main nebula. It is not inner [O III] core-shell kinematics, complete halo coverage, a filled PPV cube, or measured molecular density. A surface comparator needs an explicit velocity law and beam treatment; sparse offsets do not measure front/back position.

The original column-density and fractional-abundance columns are inferred under chemical/excitation assumptions (§4.2), including rotational temperature 10 K and an adopted H2 column. They are retained only under the separate inferred field and are excluded from velocity-fit inputs.

No calibrated per-point centroid uncertainties, spatial-error estimates or fit-covariance matrices are available here. Residual scales chosen from beam size or spectral resolution are modeling assumptions, not statistical errors from this table.
